correctness.rationale: The uniform law has exactly binomial(n-1,k-1) outcomes; zero-shifted stars and bars yields explicit ordinary generating functions for E[U], E[A], and E[UA]. An algebraically checked formal-series identity reduces the covariance to (2(k-1)/((n-1)D)) times ((k-3)h_(m-2)-h_(m-3)); all parameters, including k=1 and k=2 and parity boundaries, are handled. Nonnegative coefficient monotonicity proves strict signs for k>=5; explicit even-only expansions prove k=3 and k=4. The standalone independent verifier exhaustively enumerates n<=18 and checks exact moment identities through n<=140 (19,745 assertions). Enumeration is a check, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Searches of the published mathematical record and accessible previous findings did not locate the joint unit-part/adjacent-equality covariance sign theorem. Close work provides level-count enumeration, Carlitz (no-equality) laws, or longest equal-run laws. The new result is a complete finite all-parameter mixed covariance sign classification with nontrivial k=3/4 parity boundary. The 1998 predecessor was not readable in full and remains an explicit priority risk.

value.rationale: The number of unit parts and the number of adjacent ties are natural complementary local/global statistics of a uniformly random ordered integer composition. Their joint sign is not fixed by individual enumerations or by naive dependence intuition: it changes sharply from negative for two/three parts at even size to positive at four/five parts, with exact parity-zero boundaries. The complete classification covers all positive sizes and lengths, not a handpicked slice, and may inform analyses that combine part-frequency and local repetition statistics. It does not claim downstream theorems for other composition models.
